item.title: Start Here
item.description:
Howdy! I’m Will, a mechanical engineering student at Texas A&M. I also spend a lot of my time on electronics and embedded systems, plus anything else where I get to design something from scratch.

This site is a portfolio and a logbook. Projects are ordered with the most substantial work at the top. Click through any of them for the full story.

item.title: SAE Aero Design Team
item.description:
Structures engineer on the Texas A&M SAE Aero Design Regular Class team since May 2025. I owned the nose structure: a topology-optimized balsa truss that carried the motors and nose gear through a full season with zero structural failures. Since September 2026 I’m Product Owner for Structures, co-leading the 9-engineer structures subteam for the 2026-27 airframe.

STATUS: ‘25-‘26 season: 5th overall at SAE Aero East. ‘26-‘27 season in progress as Product Owner, Structures.

item.title: Plasma Cutter
item.description:
A Torchmate CNC plasma cutter sat unused for five years before landing in our shop. Then it became my problem to solve.

STATUS: Fully operational. 34-page SOP published, eight staff trained, in regular use for student and capstone jobs.

item.title: ATmega32U4
item.description:
A custom ATmega32U4 dev board designed in Altium, manufactured by JLCPCB. USB-C fought back. ICSP won.

STATUS: V1.1 built and working over ICSP. USB-C never enumerated; root cause not confirmed.

item.title: PBA (Custom BJT 3D Printer)
item.description:
A PhD student handed me four steel brackets epoxied together and asked me to make a plate go up and down. The actual goal: a binder-jet 3D printer that survives an autoclave.

STATUS: Shelved August 2025. Between a ridiculous amount of feature creep, and SAE Aero kicking off, I ran out of time.

item.title: Li-ion Battery Charger
item.description:
A custom single-cell Li-ion charger / boost / protection PCB. Worked for charging. Worked for boosting. The protection circuit got the MOSFET backwards.

STATUS: Shelved January 2025. Replaced by off-the-shelf modules for the projects I would’ve used it on.

item.title: Alarm Clock
item.description:
My iPhone’s alarm stopped going off one too many times. So naturally, I tried to build my own. Many lessons learned later, I have the tools to soon make my return to this project.

STATUS: V2 PCB built; its I2C bus never came up. V3 on an ATmega32U4 is planned.

item.title: A4988 Stepper Motor Controller
item.description:
A custom four-channel A4988 stepper driver board, designed mostly so I could batch-order another PCB that month. Adafruit sells the same chip on a breakout for $5. That’s the lesson.

STATUS: Built, never got a stepper to move with it. Retired in favor of off-the-shelf driver modules.

item.title: LF3DP
item.description:
A large format pellet-extrusion 3D printer built at the RPS, based on Dr. D. Flo’s open-source LF3DP design. I owned the gantry build through early 2025, then handed it off.

STATUS: Partial assembly. X-axis carriage built, waiting on machinist to trim the C-channel extrusion and install electronics. Will not finish before I graduate.
